overview:
Heart failure occurs when the heart muscle doesn't pump blood as well as it should. When this happens, blood often backs up and fluid can build up in the lungs, causing shortness of breath. Some heart conditions slowly leave the heart too weak or stiff to fill and pump blood properly, including narrowed arteries in the heart and high blood pressure.
Proper treatment may improve symptoms and help some people live longer. Lifestyle changes can improve quality of life. But heart failure can be life-threatening. Some people may need a heart transplant or a device to help the heart pump blood. Heart failure may also be called congestive heart failure.
ecg_limitations: bundle branch block can complicate accurate diagnosis of other heart conditions, especially heart attacks

common: shortness of breath with activity or when lying down
swelling in the legs ankles and feet
cough that does not go away
cough that brings up white or pink mucus with spots of blood
very rapid weight gain from fluid buildup
red_flags: rapid or irregular heartbeat with shortness of breath chest pain or fainting
sudden severe shortness of breath and coughing up white or pink foamy mucus

causes: other diseases such as diabetes HIV infection overactive or underactive thyroid or buildup of iron or protein
heart muscle damage from infections heavy alcohol use recreational drug use or some chemotherapy medicines
any illness that affects the whole body
viruses that attack the heart muscle
risk_factors: some diabetes medicines such as rosiglitazone or pioglitazone
medicines used to treat high blood pressure cancer blood conditions irregular heartbeats nervous system diseases mental health conditions lung and urinary conditions and infections
complications: heart changes that damage heart valves and cause irregular heartbeats

history_questions: Do you experience shortness of breath?
Do you have swelling in your legs or belly?
Have you gained weight rapidly in the last few days?
Do you have risk factors such as high blood pressure coronary artery disease or diabetes?
When did you first notice your symptoms?
Do your symptoms occur all the time or do they come and go?
What seems to improve your symptoms?
What seems to worsen your symptoms?
physical_exam: listening to lungs and heart with a stethoscope
checking for swelling in legs and belly

goals: treat the cause of heart failure
lifestyle: check legs ankles and feet for swelling daily
ask how much fluids you can drink
medications: angiotensin receptor plus neprilysin inhibitor sacubitril-valsartan

prevention: treat and control coronary artery disease
treat and control high blood pressure
when_to_seek_help: rapid or irregular heartbeat with shortness of breath chest pain or fainting
sudden severe shortness of breath and coughing up white or pink foamy mucus
sudden worsening symptoms if you already have heart failure
new symptoms if you already have heart failure
gain 5 pounds or more within a few days

source_notes: Heart failure may start in the left ventricle, the main pumping chamber, but can affect the right ventricle or both sides
Right-sided heart failure can cause fluid backup into the belly legs and feet
Left-sided heart failure can cause fluid backup in the lungs and shortness of breath
HFrEF is a type of left-sided heart failure where the left ventricle cannot squeeze as strongly
HFpEF is a type of left-sided heart failure where the left ventricle cannot relax or fill fully
NYHA classification uses Classes 1 to 4 based on symptoms and activity limitation
ACC/AHA staging uses Stages A to D from risk factors without symptoms to advanced heart failure
If both right and left bundle branches are blocked, the heart may beat very slowly and may require a pacemaker
Bundle branch block can complicate accurate diagnosis of heart attacks
If you have heart failure, your healthcare professional may adjust medicine doses more frequently when a new medicine starts or symptoms worsen
Hospital treatment may include medicines to relieve symptoms, medicines to help the heart pump better, and oxygen
Some people with severe heart failure may need long-term supplemental oxygen
Palliative care can reduce symptoms and improve quality of life in serious illness
Hospice care may be recommended when medicines no longer work and transplant or device therapy is not an option
